idiom_name: plain header structs plus a handler wrapper (kafka-go Header, NATS-style map headers)
implementation_notes: Go's message metadata is already plain data - kafka-go's Header is a {Key string; Value []byte} pair and NATS/HTTP-style clients use map[string][]string - so the classic history class disappears: keep one "history" header value, decode the hop slice, append this component's entry and re-encode it. The idiomatic interception point is a function that wraps the handler (or a middleware func in the router chain), so no component implements history logic itself. Context values do not cross the wire, so in-process correlation must be re-established from the header on receive.
pitfalls: kafka.Header.Value is []byte: appending a second header with the same key creates duplicates that consumers expose as an unordered slice - replace the single history value instead of adding one header per hop.
context.Context values stop at the process boundary, so a handler that reads the trail from context alone will see an empty history on the next hop; read it from the message headers.
A []byte header counts against the broker's maximum message size, so bound the list (and prefer a compact encoding) before a retry loop inflates it.
